reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about thermodynamic stabilization by configurational entropy in high-entropy nanoalloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers the general role of entropy in free energy, but the specific application to nanoalloy stability at high temperatures requires empirical backing, which is absent here.
premises: High configurational entropy thermodynamically stabilizes a single-phase solid solution in high-entropy alloys.
This stabilization suppresses phase separation and chemical segregation at high temperatures.
The effect is specifically operative in nanoalloys under high-temperature conditions.
Conventional alloys with lower configurational entropy will exhibit significant phase separation under the same conditions.
